resolution.note: Rule test scans tracked agent config for token shapes

title: Refuse committed agent settings that carry secrets
body:
Outcome: `npm run fast` and CI refuse a tracked .claude/settings*.json, .codex config or .mcp.json that holds a token-shaped value (API keys, bearer tokens, GitHub/Anthropic/OpenAI/Cloudflare token prefixes) in env or headers.
Why: Ars Technica 2026-11 (https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/claude-code-settings-files-expose-thousands-of-secrets-on-github/, found by the rss radar 2026-11-09): Claude Code settings files leak thousands of secrets on GitHub. KRN tracks .claude/settings.json and the global contract says never persist secrets.
Proof: a test seeds a settings file with a fake token and expects the check to fail naming the file and key, and the real tracked files pass.
Scope: scripts or test/rules, the CI check that already lints tracked config.
